tasks.title: Listed private manual incidents keep their ledger keys across retention expiry
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, all What each file gets bullets, acceptance 1-9 and Completion evidence; Decisions 1-5, Required behavior R1-R4, Counterexamples C1-C12, Performance impact steps 1-3 and Security impact. Add ManualIncidentsResult.listedIds using the existing descriptor-based safeId before the privacy guard and accepted incident ids; return an empty set on 404. Replace #visibleManual only after successful non-404 reads; preserve last-good and undefined semantics. Use listedIds only for pruning, never seeding, detection, routing or payloads. Keep ledger format 4, Ledger.prune, retention timing, dependencies and normal sending unchanged. Add the injected-clock internal/draft retention regressions, all event keys, pruned control, restart, absence versus failure, private-first publication, malformed listed items and safe-id cases. Preserve existing privacy and compatibility assertions, and verify a genuinely new public update is sent once after republication. Measure test CPU A/B, retention prune counts/CPU/RSS and private-feed fetch CPU as specified; put the results in the PR and leave stack measurements to the nightly api bench after merge. Keep measurement scripts outside the repository and do not raise budgets. Update docs/operation.md with listed private/malformed retention and the omitted-item limit. test/manual-incidents.test.ts needs changes only if C6/C7 coverage is missing; README.md needs changes only if its existing wording becomes wrong, as allowed by the section.

acceptance.expected: Before the production fix, run the new regression against notify f5007bfd5497035152e075d733124ca4cac87a9f. Acceptance 1 fails because ledger.has("all", "manual:9:opened") is false instead of true, or republication writes 2 lines instead of 1. Capture the failing run for the PR. A coverage-only failure is not evidence of the defect.

acceptance.command: bun test test/manual-flip.test.ts test/api.test.ts test/manual-incidents.test.ts test/feeds.test.ts test/prune.test.ts
acceptance.expected: After the fix: 0 fail. Acceptance 1 uses one clock injected into Ledger and Notifier, retention 1 day, an initial empty feed, and all/web file channels. At START + 3 * DAY both channels retain manual:9:opened, while manual:50:opened seeded at START is absent, proving pruning ran; republication leaves exactly ["manual:9:opened"] per channel. Acceptance 2 retains all 3 opened/update/resolved keys across the draft flip, with exactly 3 total lines per channel after republication; a later eligible prune after successful [] removes them (C8), whereas 500 or 404 keeps the last good presence (C9). Before any good manual read, manual keys remain protected (C10). Restart from the same ledger path adds 0 lines (acceptance 3). A draft-only id has no ledger key before publication and exactly 1 opened delivery per eligible channel afterward (C6/C7). Malformed listed safe ids retain keys (C3); string, fractional, unsafe and missing ids add no protection (C5). C12 returns rejected [{index:3,id:5,reason:"invalid"}], incidents [manualIncident({id:4})] and listedIds {1,2,4,5} for the spec's exact fixture. Existing acceptance 6 assertions remain unchanged, including private skipped count 0 then malformed-public count 1 and older-api compatibility. A new public update after republication is delivered exactly once (R4). Focused coverage may fail its threshold despite 0 failed tests; the full-suite coverage gate is checked separately.

exit 0 with Bun 1.4.0: lint, typecheck and the complete test suite pass; line coverage is at least 80% and cognitive complexity stays within 15 per function. Shared tooling, coverage thresholds and existing acceptance 6 assertions are unchanged.

Acceptance 8: prepare the named temporary file-channel config, fresh ledger path and local fake-api URL. Let the initial empty manual feed establish the channel, then serve one public manual incident and the same id as internal. Exactly 1 line is written to the channel file. Stop the service cleanly and record the actual resolved command and result. The injected-clock regression, rather than this smoke, proves retention expiry.

acceptance.command: for pulse_737_round in 1 2 3 4 5; do (cd "$PULSE_737_BASELINE_DIR" && /usr/bin/time -f '%U %S' bun run test) || exit; /usr/bin/time -f '%U %S' bun run test || exit; done
acceptance.expected: Acceptance 9 / Performance impact step 1: prepare PULSE_737_BASELINE_DIR as a separate notify checkout at f5007bfd5497035152e075d733124ca4cac87a9f, with the same Bun 1.4.0 and locked dependencies; run from the implementation checkout. All 10 full-suite runs pass. Alternate A then B 5 times on the same machine, sum user + sys for each run, and report median A, median B and B - A in seconds. The measured median B - A is <= 0.25 s, the literal cap in the spec. If over that cap, reduce the new tests' CPU cost using shared fixtures and the injected clock, then rerun; never raise budgets or weaken coverage. This local measurement matches the CPU definition in api/bench/run.ts:165-166 and api/bench/measure.ts:47-48.

Acceptance 9 / Performance impact step 2: create this throwaway script outside the repository and do not commit it. For each case use a fresh temporary ledger with one injected clock at T0; seed 1000 ids x 3 literal keys (manual:<id>:opened, manual:<id>:update:x, manual:<id>:resolved) x 2 channels = 6000 settled entries. Move the clock to T0 + 2 * 86400000, run Bun.gc(true), and call ledger.prune(86400000, new Set(), presence). Case (a), presence = new Set(), returns exactly 6000; case (b), presence = the 1000 ids, returns exactly 0. These expectations are literals from the spec, never derived from the implementation. Report process.cpuUsage() delta for each prune and RSS in MiB after a second Bun.gc(true), plus RSS (b) - (a). Report the expected few-MiB scale for 6000 seeded rows without gating RSS; seeded rows have no notification payload, so their RSS is a lower bound. Close the ledgers and clean up temporary directories. Ledger code is unchanged, so both presence-set cases run on the implementation checkout.

Acceptance 9 / Performance impact step 2: create this throwaway script outside the repository and do not commit it. Serve a JSON array of exactly 1000 internal manual items using Bun.serve on 127.0.0.1 port 0, with the existing required wire headers. Measure process.cpuUsage() around fetchManualIncidents for 20 calls on A (f5007bfd5497035152e075d733124ca4cac87a9f) and 20 on B on the same machine. Report both median CPU times per call and B - A; B - A is < 1 ms, the literal bound in the spec. Close the local server. Performance impact step 3: leave startup, load, RSS and image stack metrics to the nightly api bench after merge; do not run bench/run.ts as a notify-branch comparison because it cannot select different notify refs for A and B.

acceptance.command: git diff -- src/api.ts src/notifier.ts test/manual-flip.test.ts test/api.test.ts test/manual-incidents.test.ts docs/operation.md README.md
acceptance.expected: Review against the spec's Security impact checklist and Decisions 1-5: only own numeric safe-integer ids enter the presence set, with no coercion or getter execution; no private content or private id is added to logs, metrics, payloads or ledger rows; existing body/size limits remain unchanged. listedIds only controls pruning, replaces the last successful set and does not create keys. Ledger format remains 4 and no ledger code or dependency pin changes. Retention docs state that listed private/malformed items retain keys and omitted items are unprotected. Leave the conditionally listed test/manual-incidents.test.ts and README.md unchanged if their existing coverage/wording suffices.

Completion evidence: the PR body names #737, links the failing acceptance 1 run on f5007bfd5497035152e075d733124ca4cac87a9f and the passing run, includes bun run check output and the resolved smoke command with exactly 1 output line, records the applicable security checklist results, and states the spec's known limit that an item omitted from the API feed is not protected. It also gives acceptance 9 results: both test_cpu_s medians and B - A (<= 0.25 s), literal prune counts 6000 and 0, prune CPU and post-GC RSS for both cases and their RSS difference, and both fetch CPU medians and B - A (< 1 ms). It states that startup/load/RSS/image stack metrics are left to the nightly api bench after merge; no budget is raised and no scratch measurement script is committed.
